Title: Wee1 is a novel independent prognostic marker of poor survival in post-chemotherapy ovarian carcinoma effusions.

Journal/Date: Gynecologic oncology (2014)

MeSH Keywords: Adult, Aged, Aged, 80 and over, Ascitic Fluid, Biomarkers, Tumor, Cell Cycle Proteins, Cells, Cultured, Female


--- ABSTRACT ---
[OBJECTIVE]: Wee1-like kinase (Wee1) is a tyrosine kinase which negatively regulates entry into mitosis at the G2 to M-phase transition and has a role in inhibition of unscheduled DNA replication in S-phase. The present study investigated the clinical role of Wee1 in advanced-stage (FIGO III-IV) ovarian serous carcinoma.
[METHODS]: Wee1 protein expression was analyzed in 287 effusions using immunohistochemistry. Expression was analyzed for association with clinicopathologic parameters, including survival. Forty-five effusions were additionally studied using Western blotting. Wee1 was further silenced in SKOV3 and OVCAR8 cells by siRNA knockdown and proliferation was assessed.
[RESULTS]: Nuclear expression of Wee1 in tumor cells was observed in 265/287 (92%) and 45/45 (100%) effusions by immunohistochemistry and Western blotting, respectively. Wee1 expression by immunohistochemistry was significantly higher in post-chemotherapy disease recurrence compared to pre-chemotherapy effusions obtained at diagnosis (p=0.002). Wee1 silencing in SKOV3 and OVCAR8 cells reduced proliferation. In univariate survival analysis of the entire cohort, a trend was observed between high (>25% of cells) Wee1 expression and poor overall survival (p=0.083). Survival analysis for 109 patients with post-chemotherapy effusions showed significant association between Wee1 expression and poor overall survival (p=0.004), a finding which retained its independent prognostic role in Cox multivariate analysis (p=0.003).
[CONCLUSIONS]: Wee1 is frequently expressed in ovarian serous carcinoma effusions, and its expression is significantly higher following exposure to chemotherapy. The present study is the first to report that Wee1 is an independent prognostic marker in serous ovarian carcinoma.


[FULL TEXT STATUS]: Open-access full text is NOT available on PMC/PubTator for this PMID. Analysis must rely solely on the Abstract above, or search for alternative PMIDs with full-text availability.

key_findings.finding: The direct study is Slipicevic et al., Gynecologic Oncology 2014 (PMID 25093290), titled “Wee1 is a novel independent prognostic marker of poor survival in post-chemotherapy ovarian carcinoma effusions.” It studied advanced FIGO III–IV ovarian serous carcinoma, with WEE1 nuclear protein assessed by immunohistochemistry in 287 effusions; 45 were additionally tested by Western blot. WEE1 was detected in 265/287 (92%) by IHC and 45/45 (100%) by Western blot, and expression was higher in post-chemotherapy recurrence effusions than in pretreatment diagnostic effusions (p=0.002).

source_tools.relevance: Direct study abstract with subtype, stage, cohort, assay, and timing

key_findings.finding: For the clinically relevant post-chemotherapy subset, 109 patients with post-chemotherapy effusions were analyzed; high WEE1 expression (>25% tumor cells) was associated with significantly poorer overall survival (univariate p=0.004) and remained independently prognostic in Cox multivariable analysis after adjustment for clinicopathologic variables (p=0.003). The abstract does not report a hazard ratio or confidence interval, so an exact HR cannot be established from the available record.

The finding is specific to post-chemotherapy ovarian serous carcinoma effusions and should not be generalized to all ovarian carcinoma specimens: in the entire 287-effusion cohort, the association between high WEE1 and overall survival was only a trend (p=0.083), whereas significance emerged in the 109-patient post-chemotherapy subgroup.

source_tools.relevance: Direct comparison of entire cohort versus post-chemotherapy subgroup

key_findings.finding: Available searches found no separate primary ovarian-effusion study that independently validates or contradicts the prognostic result. Two reviews cite or summarize the same Slipicevic study, including the higher post-platinum expression and survival association, but are corroboration by secondary literature rather than independent cohorts (PMIDs 34639030 and 33224881). Other retrieved ovarian WEE1 papers were mechanistic/therapeutic or genomic-signature studies, not direct validation of WEE1 protein as an independent prognostic marker in post-chemotherapy effusions.

source_tools.relevance: Search identifying reviews and absence of a second direct effusion-prognosis cohort

The accessible abstract does not report a hazard ratio or confidence interval.
No separate primary validation cohort for this specific post-chemotherapy effusion setting was identified.
